$comment: A FUNCTION TYPE CARRIES AN ARRAY OF UNKNOWN SIZE (P69 fold f26b, lane cs; D-C-A-POINTER-TO-AN-ARRAY-OF-UNKNOWN-SIZE-IS-WARNED-INCOMPATIBLE). Two function types are compatible when their results and each parameter are (C 6.7.6.3p15), and an array of unknown or variable size is compatible with one of any size of a compatible element (C 6.7.6.2p6), so a function designator returning `int (*)[]` decays into a pointer to a function returning `int (*)[3]` or `int (*)[m]` and the reverse, a parameter the same, one function further down the same, through an initialization, an assignment, a call argument and a return statement; `==` pairs such a pointer with such a designator, `_Generic` selects the compatible association, and a function may be declared one way and defined the other. Before this fold DSS warned every designator conversion here an incompatible pointer conversion (the decay asked for the IDENTICAL signature) and `forbidDiagnostics` pins that it no longer does. Each check returns its own number on failure; 42 means every one held. The `release` arm runs the same through the shipped optimizer.
